newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain govt says not decided on petrol surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Spain govt says not decided on petrol surcharge.

text.p: The Spanish government has not made any decision on whether to maintain or remove a petrol surcharge of two pesetas per litre, an industry ministry source told Reuters.
Speculation that the government plans to remove the surcharge, which goes directly to the companies, has been one factor weighing on the share price this year of energy group Repsol, analysts said.
The surcharge was imposed some years ago along with a petrol price capping system.
"There is nothing decided", the source said.
Press reports have indicated that the administration was considering using the surcharge -- orginally imposed to help finance the entry of competition in distribution -- to swell state coffers.

Following Repsol's announcement on Monday that it is cutting its petrol prices to the public by up to two pesetas a litre, some analysts now consider that there will be no future changes in the fixing of the price of petrol.

"Repsol has sent the government a message that (it is) collaborating on inflation by cutting its prices," said one analyst, who added that it would now be more difficult for the government to justify using the surcharge to fill the public purse.
